title: Load a film pack into an instax mini 12: back unlocked, yellow marks together, back shut, lens ON, film cover ejected
instruction: Load the new film pack into the instant camera and get it ready to shoot: press the back cover lock down and open the back cover, put the pack in with its yellow mark at the camera's yellow mark and its back (with the two holes) facing out, without pressing the holes, close the cover until it locks, turn the lens ring to ON, and press the shutter button once to eject the black film cover.
context: Instant cameras are among the best-selling cameras in the US, and loading a new pack is the step every owner repeats. Fujifilm's instax mini 12 guide: slide the back cover lock down to open the back cover; insert the pack with the yellow marks aligned; close the back cover; turn the lens ring to ON; press the shutter button and the film cover is ejected. Its printer manuals add: never press the two rectangular holes on the back of the pack. A pack in upside down, a cover that isn't locked, or pressed holes means fogged or jammed film; a shutter press on a camera not loaded right ejects nothing.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, heights above the table. An instax mini 12 camera (10.4 wide along x, 6.7 deep along y, 12.2 tall; mint green; fixed), centred at x 38, y 0, standing on its base, back towards the right arm (-y), lens towards the left arm (+y). On the back: a hinged back cover (3 mm plate, 30 g) hinged along its far edge (x 43.2), swinging open towards -y to a stop at 95 degrees; under it the film chamber (6.7 wide, 9.8 tall, 2.05 deep, floor 1.1 cm up, dark; solid walls on all four sides, no finger notches), a yellow mark at its top far corner. Back cover lock: a grey tab 1.2 x 1.2 x 0.7 cm on the back at the top towards the arms (x 34-35.2, top 11.9 cm up), sprung up, 3 mm travel. Front: lens ring (silver, 6.2 across, 2.2 deep, centre x 38.6, 4.8 up) turning up to 80 degrees clockwise as seen from the front; shutter button (silver, 1.8 across, 4 mm proud, 2.5 mm travel) at x 34.6, 9.2 up. Film ejection slot on the top, front. A film pack (9.2 x 6.1 x 2.0 cm, 45 g, black; two grey holes (each 2.0 cm along its length, 1.0 cm across, centred mid-length and 1.6 cm either side of the long centre line) and a yellow corner mark on its back) lies flat, back up, centred at x 24, y -18, its length along y, yellow end away from the arms.
scoring: Seated: the pack in the chamber with its yellow end up and its back out (each axis within 10 degrees), standing on the chamber floor and centred across it (each within 3.5 mm), its back within 1.5 mm of flush. Locked: the cover pushed shut within 2 degrees with the lock tab up. ON: ring turned 30 degrees or more. Holes touched: in a real trial, a 3 x 2 cm square of household aluminium foil is taped over each hole before the trial, and a close-up photo after it shows any dent, crease or tear in the foil inside a hole's 2.0 x 1.0 cm outline (unsupported there, the foil dents under any press; over the pack's plastic it does not); in the sim, any part of either gripper finger (pads or body) comes within 0.5 mm of a hole's area at any time. 1.0: the film cover ejected by a shutter press made with the pack seated, the cover locked and the ring at ON; still so, both grippers 2 cm clear of the camera, the pack still; held 1 s. 0.75: seated, locked and ON, not yet ejected (or a hand near). 0.5: seated and locked. 0.25: seated. 0: anything else, including a pack in the chamber the wrong way round, the holes touched, and the cover ever pulled 5 degrees open while locked.
reset_notes: Camera with no pack, back cover shut and locked, lens ring at OFF, film cover inside. The pack flat on the table, back up, as in the setup photo. Real trials: a spent pack can stand in; tape a fresh 3 x 2 cm square of household aluminium foil over each of its holes before every trial, and photograph both squares close up after it.
fidelity: Camera fixed; cover, lock, ring, shutter and film cover on joints. Locked, the cover is held shut; tab 2 mm down, it springs 20 degrees ajar; shut with the tab up, it relocks. A press on a ready camera drives the film cover 4.5 cm out. The pack is one rigid box, holes drawn. No camera was measured: the chamber is the pack's size plus 3 mm a side and 0.5 mm deep, solid walls, no notches, so fingers can't enter it. Body size from Fujifilm; pack size from Wikipedia; the rest estimates.
